# Business Need

`sales.obj.core.business_need` · v1.0.0 · **draft** · scope **core**

> The outcome the buyer is trying to reach, stated in their own metrics. Distinct from Pain Point on tense and direction: pain is what hurts now, need is what better looks like. The test is whether it can be written as "from X to Y by Z" using a number the buyer already reports on — if it cannot, it is a preference wearing business language. A solution mapped to pain without a need has nothing to be measured against after the sale, which is why deals that closed on a compelling problem statement so often churn at the first renewal: nobody ever agreed what winning would look like, so nobody can show it happened.


Also called: `Desired Outcome`, `Business Objective`, `Requirement`, `Success Criteria`

## Constraints

- **`bn.metric_must_be_theirs`** target_metric must be a KPI the buyer already reports on.A metric we invented cannot be tracked after the sale and will not appear in their review.
- **`bn.delta_requires_a_baseline`** target_value is meaningless without baseline_value;the pair is atomic.
- **`bn.need_requires_a_pain`** A need with no pain point behind it may be recorded butmay not carry funding confidence. Aspirations are cut first. _(soft)_
- **`bn.horizon_is_the_buyers`** must_have_by is set from the buyer's obligation, neverback-filled from our quarter end.


## Business rules

- **`bn.no_metric_no_proposal`** A business need with no target_metric may not be the basis of a proposal. There is nothing to measure the sale against afterwards, and post-sale value reviews without a metric become arguments about memory.

- **`bn.value_claim_requires_a_baseline`** financial_value may not be asserted without baseline_value. Without a baseline the delta is invented, and the buyer's finance team will be the ones to establish that.

- **`bn.vendor_modelled_value_must_be_labelled`** Where value_basis is vendor_modelled or assumed, the figure carries that label everywhere it appears, including in slides.
- **`bn.sponsor_change_voids_the_mandate`** When champion_change is observed, sponsor_ref, mandate_source and priority_rank must be re-verified before the need is treated as live. Objectives belong to people, not to seats, and the successor almost always arrives with their own.

- **`bn.freeze_does_not_change_the_target`** A budget freeze changes time_horizon and nothing else. Re-running discovery after the fiscal turn wastes the only durable asset the deal produced.

- **`bn.success_criteria_before_commit`** A deal may not be forecast as committed while success_criteria_agreed is false. One email before signature; a renewal negotiation after it.

## Actions

- **Ask which number this is measured on** (human) — Convertsa stated outcome into a measurable one. The question sellers replace with a value-pillar slide.
- **Capture the current value** (human) — Makes the deltareal and makes the post-sale review possible. Costs one question during discovery and is unrecoverable afterwards.
- **Build the value model with the buyer** (human) — Movesvalue_basis to jointly_modelled. A number the sponsor helped produce is one they will defend in a review we cannot attend.
- **Establish where the pressure comes from** (human) — Separatesa regulator or board mandate from a team initiative, which predicts slip risk better than any pipeline stage.
- **Ask what else is competing for the budget** (human) — Names the actual opponent. Most deals are lost to the buyer's third priority, and nobody records it.
- **Agree written success criteria before signature** (human) — Sets success_criteria_agreed. One email now, or a renewal argument in twelve months.
- **Diarise a re-approach at the fiscal turn** (human) — The highest-conversion outbound available, because the need is documented and the competitor is starting from nothing.


## Evidence

- **document** · 9500 bp — The buyer's own board pack, OKR sheet or evaluationcriteria. Written for an internal audience, so it is what they actually intend to be judged on.
- **contract** · 9000 bp — Service levels and success criteria already committedto elsewhere. Binding, dated and unarguable.
- **meeting_transcript** · 8500 bp — The sponsor stating the metric unprompted.Strongest conversational evidence and currently unmined.
- **crm** · 6000 bp — Recorded close date and forecast category. Reflectsour beliefs about the need at least as much as theirs.
- **email** · 6000 bp — Written confirmation of a target. Reliable when presentand rarely present, since numbers move to attachments.
- **website** · 4000 bp — Investor guidance and published objectives. Excellentfor hypothesising the outcome, never sufficient to assert it.
- **derived** · 3000 bp — Momentum and slip signals. Corroborate urgency;say nothing at all about the metric.


## Metrics

- **quantified_need_rate** (percent) — Share of open opportunities carrying a metric,a baseline and a target.
- **buyer_modelled_value_rate** (percent) — Share where value_basis is buyer orjointly modelled. The clearest proxy for business-case durability.
- **time_to_quantify** (days) — bn.stated to bn.quantified. Long tails predictdeals that die in the finance review.
- **criteria_agreement_rate** (percent) — Share of won deals with written successcriteria. Correlates with renewal more strongly than deal size.
- **need_survival_rate** (percent) — Share of needs surviving a sponsor change.Reads directly on org_level and mandate_source.
- **value_realisation_gap** (percent) — Promised delta against measured delta atfirst renewal. The only honest calibration of every value claim above.


## Examples

- **"Cut month-end close from 11 days to 5 by Q3, because the board sees the numbers late"** — The complete shape: metric, baseline, target, date, mandate. Everything after the sale can be measured against it and the sponsor can defend it without us.
- **"We need better visibility"** — THE CLASSIC MISCLASSIFICATION. A stated outcome withno metric, filed as a business need because it sounds like one. It survives discovery, fails the finance review, and the loss is recorded as price.
- **"Reduce onboarding time" with a pain point behind it and no baseline** — Half a need.Nobody can say afterwards whether it worked, so the renewal turns on relationship rather than results.
- **DORA operational-resilience compliance by the regulatory deadline** — mandate_sourceregulator. The date is not the buyer's to move, discount pressure is weak, and the competitor is the internal build team.
- **A VP's personal efficiency initiative, org_level team, sponsor eight months in role** — Real, funded, and structurally fragile. It disappears with the sponsor, and org_level predicts that better than any warmth in the relationship.

> Eleven inference patterns: five executable today, six blocked. Every executable pattern reads the need indirectly through commercial and calendar events — budget approval, freezes, slips, sponsor changes — because the substrate can observe money moving and cannot observe the number the money is meant to change. The single highest-value signal gap is obs_kind `metric_stated` paired with fact paths need.target_metric, need.baseline_value and need.target_value (L2): it unblocks two patterns here directly, is the precondition for every post-sale value measurement in Layer 6, and its absence is why a system that can see a contract being requested still cannot say what the contract is supposed to achieve. Second is obs_kind `competing_initiative` — the buyer's own roadmap is the most frequent winner of enterprise deals and Layer 2 has no word for it.
